Pikliz

Served at: Fete de Papa Zaka - Feast of the Farmer Loa

About 4 cups (950 mL)Prep 25 min

Pikliz is a vibrant, spicy, and tangy pickled vegetable relish from Haiti, a staple condiment often served with fried foods like griot (fried pork) or Tassot (fried goat). For Fete de Papa Zaka, the annual celebration honoring the Lwa of agriculture and harvest, Papa Zaka, Pikliz is a common offering and accompaniment to the festive meals shared in his honor, symbolizing the bounty of the earth.

Ingredients

  • 1 small head green cabbage (about 1.5 lbs / 680g), thinly shredded
  • 2 medium carrots, peeled and julienned or grated
  • 1 medium red onion, thinly sliced
  • 1 green bell pepper, thinly sliced
  • 1 red bell pepper, thinly sliced
  • 1-3 Scotch bonnet or habanero peppers, stems removed, thinly sliced (remove seeds for less heat, wear gloves!)
  • 4-6 cloves garlic, thinly sliced
  • 1 cup (240 mL) white vinegar (5% acidity)
  • 1/4 cup (60 mL) fresh lime juice (from about 2 limes)
  • 1 tablespoon salt
  • 1 teaspoon black peppercorns
  • 4-5 whole cloves

Method

  1. In a large non-reactive bowl, combine the shredded cabbage, julienned carrots, sliced red onion, green bell pepper, red bell pepper, Scotch bonnet/habanero peppers, and sliced garlic.
  2. Using clean hands, massage the vegetables with the salt for 2-3 minutes. This helps to soften them slightly and draw out some moisture.
  3. Add the white vinegar, fresh lime juice, black peppercorns, and whole cloves to the vegetable mixture.
  4. Stir everything thoroughly to ensure all vegetables are well coated with the liquid and spices.
  5. Pack the pikliz tightly into a clean, sterile glass jar or container. Ensure the vegetables are submerged in the liquid. If needed, press down with a clean utensil or add a bit more vinegar to cover.
  6. Seal the jar and refrigerate for at least 24 hours before serving to allow the flavors to meld and the pickling process to begin. Pikliz tastes even better after a few days.

Tips

  • Adjust the amount of Scotch bonnet or habanero peppers to your preferred spice level. For less heat, remove the seeds and membranes. Always wear gloves when handling hot peppers.
  • Pikliz can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2-3 weeks. Its flavor will continue to develop over time.
  • Serve pikliz as a zesty, spicy condiment alongside fried meats (like griot or fried chicken), grilled fish, or even with rice and beans for an extra kick.
